name: MBB BK 117 (A/B/C-1)
summary: A boxy German-Japanese light twin used widely for EMS and utility; the ancestor of the EC145/H145.

wings: Short mast with a compact head
engines: Twin turboshafts side by side on the roof
Two short exhaust stubs at the rear of the humps
fuselage: Boxy pod with large clamshell doors at the rear of the cabin
Skids with a short body, boxy blunt nose
tail: Long boom with a distinctive upward kink
Horizontal stabilizer with fin end plates and a conventional tail rotor

tellTales: Compact boxy pod with rear clamshell cargo doors
Twin engines under a hump with four-blade rotor
Tail boom with a pronounced upward sweep

confusedWith.howToTell: The H145 is bigger with a longer cabin and a sleeker nose, and often has sliding doors; the BK 117 is a smaller, boxier pod.
The Bo 105 is shorter and has a more stubby look; the BK 117 is longer and has a taller cabin.
The H135 has a fenestron tail; the BK 117 has a conventional tail rotor.
